{{Quote|Think of it like Mos Eisley, but uglier, nastier and less hospitable.|[[Mirax Terrik Horn|Mirax Terrik]] to [[Gavin Darklighter]]|<ref name="X-Wing: Wedge's Gamble">''[[X-Wing: Wedge's Gamble]]''</ref>}}
The '''Alien Protection Zone''', colloquially known as the '''Invisible Sector''' or '''Invisec''' for short, was a walled-off [[ethnic neighborhood]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Imperial Center]].

==History==
Supposedly built for [[Non-huMan|non-Human]] [[Species/Legends|species]] to protect them from "genuine prejudice", the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] was, in essence, segregating them from the human population. This practice was in line with the Empire's [[Humanocentrism|Humanocentric]] policies.

Conditions inside Invisec were very poor and residents were often harassed by [[Stormtrooper/Legends|Stormtroopers]]. Propaganda reports indicated that neighborhoods were built to reflect the various different cultures of the galaxy's [[Alien/Legends|alien]] species, with neighborhoods being dominated by statues to honor heroes from their respective homeworlds. This tactic was used to make alien residents feel as if the ethnic neighborhoods were really meant to be a place of honor and hope, which they were not.

[[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] went to Invisec during the prelude to the [[Liberation of Coruscant (Galactic Civil War)|Battle of Coruscant]] in late [[6 ABY/Legends|6 ABY]]. Under the rule of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], the area was opened up. It was within Invisec that the [[Alien Combine]] movement was housed - comprising of numerous aliens, including [[Asyr Sei'lar]], future member of Rogue Squadron. Also in Invisec was the [[Azure Dianoga Cantina]], where part of the squadron gained valuable information and allies, instrumental to the success of the mission.

==Behind the scenes==
Invisec is akin in nature to the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazi_ghettos ghettos] of [[Wikipedia:Nazi Germany|Nazi Germany]] and the [[Wikipedia:Township (South Africa)|townships]] of [[Wikipedia:Apartheid|Apartheid]] [[Wikipedia:South Africa|South Africa]], both of which regimes held real-world similarities with the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].
